transform_notes: SAP's own key is the ACDOCA composite (client/ledger/company/fiscal year/document/DOCLN).

The depreciation method is implicit via the asset's own depreciation terms (ANLB-AFASL), not repeated on each posting line -- redundant with the Assets master mapping, not a separate field to load here.
Must resolve to the same staging key used in the Assets master mapping. ACDOCA carries the asset number directly on asset-relevant posting lines.

IMPORTANT GAP: a real depreciation posting is a balanced two-line document (debit depreciation expense, credit accumulated depreciation) -- the same double-entry shape as Journal Entries/General Ledger. This source table has only ONE amount per row, unlike General Ledger's paired Debit_Amount/Credit_Amount, so it can only supply one of the two required lines. The current transform engine has no 'expand one source row into a balanced multi-line posting' capability -- flagged as a real architecture gap, not worked around by fabricating an offsetting line or a plausible-looking account.
A running balance, not stored data -- same finding as General Ledger>Running_Balance and Assets>Accumulated_Depreciation; derived from the posted lines via ANLC, not loaded directly.
Same USNAM-vs-Created_By_User_ID overlap flagged on Journal Entries>Prepared_By_User_ID -- confirm which user-tracking field is actually authoritative before loading either.
May be a technical system timestamp rather than the accounting posting date already captured in Period_Date/BUDAT -- confirm the two aren't redundant before mapping both.
system-generated on posting -- not loaded as source data.
